Bill.BriefDescription: Clarifying tenant remedies upon landlord's failure to perform duties.

BillBody.BillTitle: AN ACT Relating to tenant remedies upon landlord's failure toperform duties; amending RCW 59.18.070; and creating new sections.
BillBody.EnactingClause: BE IT ENACTED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF THE STATE OF WASHINGTON:

BillSection.RCWSLText: It is the intent of the legislature toaddress the decision of the Washington court of appeals in Landis &Landis Constr. LLC v. Nation, 171 Wn. App. 157 (2012) and itsinterpretation of the Washington supreme court case Foisy v. Wyman, 83Wn.2d 22 (1973). The decision allows a tenant to state a common lawcause of action for a defective condition at the rental premises. Thetenant may decide to unilaterally walk away from the lease withoutputting the landlord on notice regarding the defective condition andallowing the landlord to remedy it. By contrast, RCW 59.18.070, a part of the residentiallandlord-tenant act, gives the tenant a remedy for defective conditionsat the rental premises, but requires the tenant to notify the landlordand to afford the landlord varying periods of time to remedy specificdefective conditions. The court of appeals opinion and its interpretation of Foisy v. p. 1 SB 6030Wyman create an irreconcilable conflict between the judgecreatedremedy for defective conditions at the premises and the remedy createdby the legislature in RCW 59.18.070. It is the intent of the legislature to establish that the remedyfor defective conditions at residential rental premises in Washingtonunder RCW 59.18.070 is paramount.

BegSecAmd.BegSecText: RCW 59.18.070 and 2010 c 8 s 19018 are each amended toread as follows:

BillSection.RCWSLText: (1) If at any time during the tenancy the landlord fails to carryout the duties required by RCW 59.18.060 or by the rental agreement,the tenant may, in addition to pursuit of remedies otherwise providedhim or her by law except as provided in subsection (2) of this section,deliver written notice to the person designated in RCW59.18.060(((14))) (15), or to the person who collects the rent, whichnotice shall specify the premises involved, the name of the owner, ifknown, and the nature of the defective condition. The landlord shallcommence remedial action after receipt of such notice by the tenant assoon as possible but not later than the following time periods, exceptwhere circumstances are beyond the landlord's control: (((1))) (a) Not more than twentyfour hours, where the defectivecondition deprives the tenant of hot or cold water, heat, orelectricity, or is imminently hazardous to life; (((2))) (b) Not more than seventytwo hours, where the defectivecondition deprives the tenant of the use of a refrigerator, range andoven, or a major plumbing fixture supplied by the landlord; and (((3))) (c) Not more than ten days in all other cases. In each instance the burden shall be on the landlord to see thatremedial work under this section is completed promptly. If completionis delayed due to circumstances beyond the landlord's control,including the unavailability of financing, the landlord shall remedythe defective condition as soon as possible. (2) The remedies provided under subsection (1) of this sectionsupersede those provided under an implied warranty of habitability.

This act applies to all causes of actioncommenced on or after the effective date of this section, regardless of SB 6030 p. 2 when the cause of action arose. To this extent, this act appliesretroactively, but in all other respects it applies prospectively.
